hooks/post_tool_tracker/ (package, 32 nodes: core.py, github_integration.py, loaders.py, progress_tracker.py, policies/*.py x6)

metadata.data_source: docs/phase-0-reverse-engineering/ast_call_graph.json (2,218 nodes, 1,686 Andersen-lite edges; the repo's own call_graph_builder.py was NOT used -- see builder_divergence.md, MAX_FILES=300 cap silently drops sdlc_pipeline/ and 38/45 hook-package files from its output)
metadata.blast_radius_tier: MEDIUM (borderline: BR=0.0609 sits just above the LOW/MEDIUM 0.05 boundary; per skill thresholds BR in [0.05,0.15) = MEDIUM). This tier is driven almost entirely by the SIZE of the two packages' own internal call structure (135 self-contained nodes), NOT by risk propagating to surviving code -- see external_dependency_verification below, which found zero HIGH-confidence edges crossing the deletion boundary in either direction.
metadata.ir_norm_note: IR_norm = affected-set risk (cyclomatic_complexity x log2(1+coupling), summed) / whole-graph risk. Computed for completeness per skill Response Rule 3; interpret alongside blast_radius_tier's caveat above.
metadata.cha_reachable_note: 93/135 (68.9%) of the affected set was already CHA-reachable (confirmed live) before this change; the remaining 42 nodes were already CHA-unreachable per Phase 0.1's dead-code scan and were dormant code even before deletion.

external_dependency_verification.method: Checked every edge in ast_call_graph.json crossing the deletion boundary (external code -> deletion group, deletion group -> retained stop_notifier, stop_notifier -> deletion group) for confidence and resolution_method.
external_dependency_verification.verdict: All 26 candidate cross-boundary edges are resolution_method=cha_only, confidence=LOW -- the graph's own weakest resolution tier. Manually verified 4 representative edges by reading source: every one is a bare-name collision (e.g. langgraph_engine.exceptions.WorkflowEngineError.__init__ appearing to call hooks.pre_tool_enforcer.registry.PolicyRegistry.__init__ is actually a super().__init__(message) call to Exception.__init__; hooks.pre-tool-enforcer.check_checkpoint_pending appearing to call hooks.stop_notifier.voice.get_current_session_id is actually a call to the sibling hooks.pre_tool_enforcer.loaders.get_current_session_id, both modules exporting a function with that name). Zero genuine external dependencies exist in either direction. This is the evidence for the 'zero direct/indirect external impact' verdict.

metadata.risk_tier_note: risk_tier on each affected node below is an INTERNAL structural score (complexity + coupling WITHIN the doomed packages) -- it identifies which functions are the most complex/central pieces of functionality being removed. It is NOT a survivor-side risk signal, since every fan-out target of a CRITICAL/HIGH-tier node here is itself also being deleted in the same change (self-contained group deletion).
metadata.cii_methodology_note: Per change-impact-analysis skill's own Anti-Patterns section ('Reusing the CII AHP weight vector... for a domain with no PII/regulatory surface... wastes the dominant weight'), the default 5-criteria AHP vector (w=[0.229,0.122,0.473,0.064,0.112], PII-dominant) was NOT reused verbatim: C3 (PII/regulatory) is 0 for every node in this change set (confirmed via audit_surface.json cross-reference below) and C5 (production traffic) has no data source in this repo. A re-derived 2-factor score was used instead: CII = 0.60*coupling_within_group + 0.40*complexity, both normalized to the affected set's own max. cr_validation is N/A for this simplified vector (CR=0.0083 applies only to the unmodified 5x5 AHP matrix, not to this 2-factor substitute).
metadata.critical_gate_reasoning: AUTOMATIC-CRITICAL trigger is 'any node in audit_surface.json that becomes unreachable'. Cross-referenced all three audit_surface.json categories (62 credential_access_sites, 17 settings_json_touch_sites, 112 subprocess_spawn_sites) against the deletion groups: credential_access_sites=0 matches, settings_json_touch_sites=0 matches, subprocess_spawn_sites=2 matches (hooks/pre_tool_enforcer/daemon.py:134, hooks/pre_tool_enforcer/policies/push_gate.py:234 -- process-spawning capability loss, not audit/credential-surface loss). Gate is NOT triggered: no credential-handling or settings.json-touching code becomes unreachable.

policy_tracking_helper_verdict.question: Is hooks/policy_tracking_helper.py hook-only, or does it have independent (non-hook) production importers?
policy_tracking_helper_verdict.verdict: HOOK-ONLY. It has NO independent production importer anywhere in the repo.
evidence: Repo-wide grep for 'policy_tracking_helper' (excluding the file itself) matches exactly: hooks/pre_tool_enforcer/core.py:53 ('from policy_tracking_helper import record_policy_execution'), hooks/post_tool_tracker/core.py:56 ('from policy_tracking_helper import get_session_id, record_policy_execution, record_sub_operation'), and five test files (tests/test_session_context.py, tests/test_pre_tool_enforcer.py, tests/test_post_tool_tracker.py, tests/test_root_scripts.py).
Both production importers (pre_tool_enforcer/core.py, post_tool_tracker/core.py) are themselves inside the two packages being deleted.
hooks/stop_notifier/ (retained) does NOT import policy_tracking_helper -- confirmed by the same grep pass; the retained Stop hook has no dependency on it.
Call-graph cross-check (analyze3.py pass) found zero edges into policy_tracking_helper from any node outside {pre_tool_enforcer_pkg, post_tool_tracker_pkg, policy_tracking_helper itself}.
policy_tracking_helper_verdict.consequence: policy_tracking_helper.py's 8 nodes become fully orphaned (dead in production, though still test-covered) as a direct consequence of the settings.json change, even though it is not itself named in the diff. Included in affected_nodes below.
